anomalies.observed: The PCA9685PW PWM driver (U2, 'PWM Driver') sits on the I2C2_FCC bus together with the INA219 (U1, also on I2C2_SCL_FCC/I2C2_SDA_FCC). U2's block annotation reads 'I2C address: 0x41', which requires its address pin A0 to be tied high, but the drawing shows A0–A5 (pins 1–6) all returned to GND (the 'GND' label/vertical wire next to the A-pin bank), i.e. address 0x40.
anomalies.expected: Per the specification the PCA9685PW is 'I2C addr 0x40'; since the INA219AIDCNR is fixed at 0x40 by its own A0/A1 strapping (both to GND, matching 'I2C addr 0x40') and both devices share I2C2, the PWM driver must not also be at 0x40. The annotation '0x41' indicates the intended strapping is A0 high (0x41), so A0 should not be grounded.

evidence.quote: PWM/servo driver | FCCPeripherals | NXP PCA9685PW (I2C 16-ch PWM), I2C addr 0x40
Current/voltage sensor | Hades (top sheet) | TI INA219AIDCNR, I2C addr 0x40, across R1 = 10 mΩ shunt
PWM Driver block, U2 PCA9685PW, 'I2C address: 0x41'; A0..A5 (pins 1-6) shown strapped to GND; U1 INA219 block on same I2C2_SCL_FCC/I2C2_SDA_FCC nets with 'I2C address: 0x40'

anomalies.impact: If both the INA219 and the PCA9685 answer at 0x40 on I2C2_FCC, the two devices collide on the bus: PWM/servo commands and voltage/current telemetry would both be unreliable, potentially preventing servo control and power monitoring.

anomalies.observed: The battery current-sense shunt is annotated 'R1 10mOhm 1W 3512' on the Power sheet, i.e. a 3512 footprint.
anomalies.expected: The specification states the shunt is 'R1 = 10 mΩ (1 W, 2512 package)', so a 2512 footprint is intended.

evidence.quote: Battery current passes through shunt R1 = 10 mΩ (1 W, 2512 package), sensed differentially by INA219AIDCNR

anomalies.impact: The larger 3512 body occupies more board area than the intended 2512 land pattern and would not fit a 2512 placement/assembly, though the electrical value (10 mΩ, 1 W) is unchanged.

parsed.summary: One likely deviation was found: the PCA9685PW (U2) is annotated as I2C address 0x41 but its address pins appear strapped to GND (0x40), which would collide with the INA219 at 0x40 on the same I2C2_FCC bus and contradicts the spec's 'I2C addr 0x40'. A secondary inconsistency is the shunt R1 package annotation (3512) versus the spec's stated 2512.
